Chelsea Odufu

Chelsea Odufu is a Guyanese–Nigerian American award-winning filmmaker and visual artist working across narrative and experimental film, video art, installation, and photography. Through Afrofuturistic imagery combined with archival material, she constructs layered narratives that interweave past, present, and future.




In 2024, New Afro presented the first episode of her satirical Afrofuturist series Black Lady Goddess in collaboration with Ciné Mayence, as part of the exhibition Restitution… et après? in Mainz (Institut Français).

Benjamin Abana

Benjamin Abana is a Copenhagen-based painter of Nigerian and Danish heritage whose expressive figurative practice explores identity and human emotion through vibrant colour palettes and striking portraiture. He gained national recognition in 2019 after winning the title of Denmark’s Best Portrait Painter on Danish national television.




His collaboration with New Afro began in 2022 in Cologne with the exhibition Basic Human Emotions. That same year, he presented his work alongside painter Francel Aris Dagbeto in Mainz as part of the exhibition Rencontre (Atelier Christiane Schauder).




This collaboration continued in 2023 in Copenhagen (Denmark)

Cheria Essieke Bayer

Cheria Essieke Bayer is a creative, living in Germany since 2013. As the founder, creative director of New Afro and independent art curator, she is committed to showcasing the richness and diversity of African cultures and artistic practices, while creating international platforms for African creatives.
